questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Physical Divisions of India' refers to.
questions.a: India's land falls into broad physical divisions: the Himalayas in the north, the northern plains watered by great rivers, the peninsular plateau, the deserts, the coastal strips and the island groups.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Physical Divisions of India'.
questions.a: Each division has its own land, climate and life, and together they make India's geography rich and distinct.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Physical Divisions of India' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Rivers of India' refers to.
questions.a: Great rivers give India its shape of life: the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra flow from the Himalayas, while the Narmada, Tapi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri drain the peninsula.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Rivers of India'.
questions.a: Rivers water the fields, carry trade and draw pilgrims, so civilisations bloom along their banks.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Rivers of India' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Reading the Physical Map of India

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Reading the Physical Map of India' refers to.
questions.a: A physical map shows mountains, plateaus, plains, rivers and seas through colour and signs; reading it lets you trace journeys from the peaks to the islands and see how the land rises and falls.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Reading the Physical Map of India'.
questions.a: Maps turn a whole subcontinent into one page you can read at a glance.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Reading the Physical Map of India' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Diversity and the Character of the Land

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Diversity and the Character of the Land' refers to.
questions.a: The chapter opens with the thought that India's very geography gives it a national character; from Himalayan snow to Kanyakumari's seas, the varied land is one home whose diversity knits the people together.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Diversity and the Character of the Land'.
questions.a: Geographical diversity is not a barrier but a bond: different lands, one country.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Diversity and the Character of the Land' taught, and from which source text?
